name: King's Crossing (King's Crossing Village)
award: 2023 Federal 4% and state housing tax credits (Round Two)
headline: Community Development Partners and Restoration Christian Ministries developed King's Crossing Village, a 179-unit intergenerational community (178 income-restricted at 30% to 80% AMI, 51 reserved for ages 55+) on church-owned parking lots in Aurora's Centretech neighborhood; it won 2023 Round Two federal 4% and state credits with $38M of CHFA bonds, broke ground in February 2025 and is leasing in October 2026.
why_it_matters: It is a model of faith-based land use for housing: a congregation ground-leases its surplus parking to an experienced developer, serves as co-general partner and service provider, and the deal layers state, city ARPA and congressional funds with a housing authority tax exemption.

status.label: Leasing (October 2026); groundbreaking 2025-02-27
status.detail: The developer announced the groundbreaking held on 2025-02-27; on 2026-10-21 the property's leasing site listed specific units available for move-in on 2026-10-19 and 2026-10-20. No certificate of occupancy or placed-in-service date was found.

next_step: Watch for the placed-in-service date of the last building and CHFA compliance records; the application had planned final completion in September 2026.

key_numbers.meaning: 54 one-, 54 two-, 54 three- and 16 four-bedroom restricted units at 30% to 80% AMI, plus one manager's unit; 51 units are reserved for ages 55+.
About $36.0M over 10 years, plus $1,100,000 of state credit.
About 55% of basis, planned to pay down to about $14.7M of long-term bonds; Citi provides the construction and permanent loans.
$7.12M from the Colorado Division of Housing, $3M of HUD congressional funding and $1M of City of Aurora ARPA funds.

facts.value: 15660 E. 6th Ave., Aurora 80011 (CHFA); the groundbreaking release gives the three buildings as 15800, 15860 and 15740 E. Sixth Ave.
Level, irregular, about 5.74-acre parcel of former parking lots next to the church's operations center, with about 570 feet of frontage on East 6th Avenue
Owned by Restoration Christian Fellowship, which entered a long-term ground lease with Community Development Partners, per the application
MU-C (Mixed Use Corridor), no maximum density under Aurora's Unified Development Ordinance

Three buildings, wood frame with glulam post and beam on post-tensioned slabs, elevators and interior corridors; 100% electric with solar, heat pump water heaters and central ERV; 13-foot over-excavation for expansive soils
2023 Qualified Census Tract; about 0.3 miles from the Chambers Road and 6th Avenue bus stop
Community for All Ages model; RCM staffs one full-time resident services coordinator and a resident services wing, with nearby daycare, cafe, employment, health and food programs
Housing Authority of the City of Aurora partnered to provide the tax exemption
Enterprise Green Communities and Energy Star (target)

money.note: CHFA issuer; the application described a CHFA-issued conduit structure with tax-exempt drawdown bonds paying down to about $14.7M long-term, private placement, no taxable bonds.
Citi; Impact Development Fund provided an additional permanent loan.

money.source: Colorado Division of Housing (State Housing Board)

money.note: Awarded in 2023 to fill a cost-increase gap.

parties.role: Co-general partner, land owner and service provider
parties.name: Restoration Christian Fellowship / Restoration Christian Ministries
Housing Authority of the City of Aurora
Apartment Management Consultants (per CDP; the application named FPI Management)

background.text: The project carries out the late founding pastor's plan to turn the church's empty parking lots into housing; the church campus has hosted Safe Parking and Safe Outdoor Space programs with the Salvation Army and the City of Aurora, and eligible residents of those programs were to be offered housing.
It is Community Development Partners' first Colorado development; the developer works in California, Oregon, Nevada and Arizona.

The market study gave an 11.2% required capture rate and a 4.7% surveyed vacancy rate, with 25 tax credit projects in the market area; the applicant said it would be the first tax credit project there using 80% AMI limits.

The application planned a December 2023 site development plan submittal, permits in November 2024, construction start in early 2025 and final placed-in-service in September 2026; the groundbreaking took place on 2025-02-27.
The applicant cited a support letter from the Aurora mayor's office and no known opposition.

discrepancies.text: CHFA lists the address as 15660 E. 6th Ave., while the groundbreaking release gives the three buildings as 15800, 15860 and 15740 E. Sixth Ave.
The application credits the $3M congressional appropriation to a U.S. House member's office, while the groundbreaking release credits a U.S. Senator's office.
The application named FPI Management as property manager, while the developer's project page names Apartment Management Consultants.
